notes: Chunk B: module M2, topics M2.S10 to M2.S16 (15 units: 9 worked, 4 pairs, 2 singles = 21 items). Book pages 6 to 13.

Rule used: a diagram is required where the book gives the figure only as a picture (the nets of Figure it Out Q1), where a verbal arrangement of squares has to be seen to be folded (cross net with labels, six squares), or where the answer IS a drawing (nets of a cuboid, all 11 nets of a cube). Count-and-name questions on solids and profiles (Build it in your imagination, faces/edges/vertices) stay text and LaTeX.

The part labels (i) to (vi) are drawn in the S15 Q1 question and solution figures and (i), (ii) in the Q3 solution figure: the question and the LP solution refer to the nets by them, so they are part of the figure and not headings.
Overlap marks in the S15 Q1 solution figure (squares that land on one face in nets (i) and (v)) were found by a fold simulation; the LP says only that a square lands on a wall.
The 11 nets in the C43 solution figure were enumerated by computer (35 hexominoes, 11 fold into a cube) and match the LP families 6 + 3 + 1 + 1.
Teaching images are not linked anywhere; concept images C22.IMG1, C23.IMG1, C24.IMG1, C26.IMG1, C29.IMG1, C32.IMG1, C37.IMG1, C38.IMG1, C39.IMG1 sit in the same concepts as the worked examples.
Base figures of pages 12 and 13 that belong to nets of other solids (P12-net-3 tetrahedron nets, P13-*) are not claimed here: they belong to chunk C (M2.S17 and later).
Page 6 (Escher print, section 4.1; Tesla portrait) has no entry in the base inventory; the Escher print belongs to the fractal-art section (chunk A), the portrait is a photograph of a person.

LP oddities: the singles C43 and C44 carry book_number 'Figure it Out, Q1' although their ncert_refs are FiO3.q2 and FiO3.q3; the LP question text of C43 drops the book's sentence 'For example, the following nets are all considered the same'.
